steps.title: First zone
steps.body: Luján de Cuyo lies just south of Mendoza city, at about 900 to 1,100 m, along the Mendoza river. It's Mendoza's historic quality heartland, sometimes called the first zone, primera zona, with Maipú. Sub-areas like Perdriel, Agrelo, Vistalba and Las Compuertas have deep alluvial soils with stones.

steps.title: Old vines and DOC
steps.body: Luján de Cuyo has some of Argentina's oldest Malbec vines, many planted before 1950, on their own roots, since phylloxera spreads slowly in Mendoza's sandy, irrigated soils. In 1989, it became Argentina's first DOC, Denominación de Origen Controlada, for Malbec. Its wines are ripe, round and generous, with soft tannins.

steps.title: Producers
steps.body: Historic and famous producers include Catena Zapata, whose founder Nicolás Catena pioneered high-altitude, quality Malbec in the 1990s, Achával-Ferrer, Norton and Terrazas de los Andes. Many large wineries are based here, with vineyards both in Luján and in the Valle de Uco.

steps.prompt: Which are sub-areas of Luján de Cuyo?
steps.explanation: Gualtallary is in the Valle de Uco.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Luján de Cuyo is Mendoza's historic quality heart
It has old, own-rooted Malbec vines
It became Argentina's first DOC in 1989
